activities.anchor: one of geology's live comparative problems
activities.caption: pair each rocky world with its tectonic regime
activities.name: planetDriftMatch

config.prompt: The drift question, asked everywhere — pair each world with its regime:

pairs.right: stagnant lid — resurfaced catastrophically, heat escaping through one lid
one plate — the Tharsis bulge grew in place for billions of years
contracting single plate — wrinkled into lobate scarps as the core cooled
mobile lid — plates that break, drift and subduct

config.why: Plate tectonics is a regime, not a default: it needs water-softened, breakable lithosphere and the right heat flow — Earth has them, its neighbours apparently do not.

activities.anchor: InSight's seismometer (2018–2022) gave Mars its first interior profile
activities.caption: sequence the dead-dynamo chain
activities.name: planetDynamoOrder

config.prompt: One world's atmospheric death, in five steps — put them in order:
items: Differentiation gives the young planet a liquid-iron outer core
The outer core runs a dynamo — a magnetic shield
About 4 billion years ago, the dynamo dies
No shield: the solar wind strips the air
The ancient southern crust stays magnetised; the younger north does not
config.why: A planetary death recorded in rock — magnetism adds the history that seismology and gravity alone cannot date.

activities.anchor: planetary cooling written directly into topography
activities.caption: call Mercury's contraction
activities.name: planetScarpEst

config.prompt: Mercury's lobate scarps record the whole planet shrinking — roughly how many kilometres of radius were lost as the huge iron core cooled?
config.why: About 7 km over billions of years — contraction readable only because the layering story said an iron core dominates a small planet.
config.context: Isostasy works everywhere: floating crust stands higher where it is thicker; unloading raises terrain.

activities.anchor: Both are differentiated, like every large body
activities.caption: place Mercury's core fraction
activities.name: planetCorePlace

config.prompt: Mercury's outsized iron core — what share of the planet's radius does it fill?
config.why: About 85% of the radius — probably a giant impact stripped its mantle. The Moon, by contrast, holds a ~300 km core and a partial melt layer. 'Dead' means the dynamo and tectonics stopped, not that the layering vanished.

activities.caption: file each volcano by its heat source
activities.name: planetHeatSort

config.prompt: Volcanism runs on different fuels — file each body:

items.label: Io — sulphur plains and plumes 300 km high, its rock flexed between Jupiter and the other moons
the Moon's mare basalts, flooding the near side 3–4 billion years ago
Olympus Mons — the Solar System's tallest volcano, ~22 km high
Hawaii — a drawn trail, island by island

config.why: Melt rises where heat and pressure interact — but the energy sources differ, and on the icy moons even the solvent switches, to water-ammonia cryovolcanism.

activities.anchor: direct evidence of active volcanism this geologic instant
activities.caption: find the faulty line — worlds we called dead
activities.name: planetAliveSpot

config.prompt: One of these claims is backwards — click it:
lines: InSight recorded well over a thousand marsquakes between 2018 and 2022.
Mars shows active dust avalanches and recurring slope streaks.
A 2023 re-analysis of Magellan radar found a Venusian vent that changed shape between 1991 images.
Old surfaces record old history, which proves the machine has stopped.
'Dead planet' is a hypothesis the data keep partially overturning.
config.correction: Old surfaces record old history — they do not prove a stopped machine; the vent changed shape between images taken 32 years apart.
config.why: The inference from cratered surfaces to dead interiors is exactly the leap the modern instruments keep catching.

activities.anchor: the opposite of Earth's isostatic quiet
activities.caption: fill the blanks — why subduction is the hard step
activities.name: planetSubductCloze

config.text: Every 'no boundaries here' world is an experiment on the hard step: %%0%% requires driving dense-enough lithosphere into the mantle — our %%1%%-softened plates manage it where the dry, buoyant lids of Venus and Mars do not; Mars's %%2%% Marineris, opened by the Tharsis load, has no subduction to ever close it.
config.hint: The process, the softener, and the canyon's name.

activities.anchor: and it is not on Earth's trajectory this century or this millennium
activities.caption: bet before the reveal — what Venus teaches
activities.name: planetVenusPredict

config.q: Venus's runaway greenhouse is often cited in climate discussions. What is the honest comparative reading?
choices: Venus is Earth's forecast — study it and you know our fate
Climates have multiple stable states with sharp transitions between them; Venus proves such transitions exist, without dating ours
config.why: Venus's fate was set by starting conditions — closer to the Sun, a different early water inventory, likely no carbon-cycle tectonics. The lesson is structural, not predictive; confusing the two is the standard error in both directions.
